gen-gf-oxanium-inter: Oxanium stands out with tall lowercase and curves that end in clear daylight, all drawn in one unbroken line. Inter follows in a plain sans with wide counters, giving the page room to breathe.
gen-gf-saira-extra-condensed-fs-erode: Letters pulled tight together, every stroke as constant as bent wire: that is Saira Extra Condensed. And Erode, a classic serif with gentle swelling in its strokes, keeps paragraphs comfortable to wade through.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-bitter: Bitter, a slab-serif with a very large lowercase eye and see-through s shapes, reads dependable and grounded. But Snowburst One, with its stenciled bridges, supplies the bold, expressive punch above it.
gen-gf-paprika-rubik: Paprika scatters its letters wide and lets the lowercase fill the line like capitals, while Rubik sits below in a plain sans. One is built to command attention; the other to stay soft and clear.
gen-gf-revalia-inter: Revalia has a lowercase g with an open lower curve and a relaxed stride across widely spaced letters, loud and expressive. Inter is the sans that stays smooth and tube-like beneath it.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-mulish: A stencil sheet with wide bridges between letters defines Snowburst One, bold and expressive with tall lowercase. Mulish then takes over as a sans with no thick-and-thin modulation, soft in its curves and open as a horseshoe magnet.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-lexend-peta: Wallpoet is bold and commanding, with high-rising lowercase and paper showing through its lines between letters. And Lexend Peta, a plain sans with curves that never thin, gives it a big-x-height, approachable partner.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-roboto-slab: Expressive and bold, Snowburst One comes stenciled with tall lowercase. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif with open throats and a dominant middle zone, brings precise structure that grounds the loud heading.
gen-gf-sofia-sans-extra-condensed-fs-ero: Tight, tall and upright, Sofia Sans Extra Condensed keeps its monoline strokes close together. But Erode, a classic serif with medium-low stress between stem and hairline, brings the dignified, editorial voice to the text.
gen-gf-tektur-bitter: Expressive and a little odd, Tektur looks traced with one marker tip, with generous openings on every curve and outsized lowercase. Bitter, a slab-serif, grounds it with a very large lowercase eye.
